title: plugin-auth: enable better-auth's one-time-token plugin so the mobile shell can hand a system-browser sign-in back to its WebView
body:
repo:mobile#1 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYnW1Xf6HDSWz1eGAqv

Filing category ③: a direct task from a maintainer ruling. objectstack-ai/mobile#148 comment 6593861138: `Ruling: batch #1 item 4 · letter B · maintainer 「同意」`. Option B reuses the auth library's existing plugin instead of hand-writing a code-exchange endpoint.

## Why

Some identity providers (Google among them) refuse embedded WebViews. A mobile user who signs in with such a provider cannot sign in to the app today: objectstack-ai/mobile#176 detects the refusal and shows "not supported in the app yet".

The ruled flow:
1. The shell opens the sign-in in the system auth session (`ASWebAuthenticationSession` on iOS, Custom Tabs on Android).
2. The server issues a single-use, short-lived code to the app scheme.
3. The Console in the WebView exchanges that code for its own session.

## The ruling's premise, measured by the seat

`better-auth@1.7.12` is the version `packages/plugins/plugin-auth` pins. Its npm tarball ships `./plugins/one-time-token`, with these endpoints:
- `/one-time-token/generate`: an authenticated session issues a token;
- `/one-time-token/verify`: the token is exchanged for a session.

Read from `dist/plugins/one-time-token`:
- default expiry 3 minutes (`expiresIn ?? 3`);
- `storeToken: "hashed"` is available;
- `disableClientRequest` exists.

On objectstack `main`, `git grep -nE "oneTimeToken|@better-auth/expo" -- packages/plugins/plugin-auth` returns 0 hits, so the plugin is not enabled today.

## Ask

- Enable the plugin in `plugin-auth`'s plugin list:
  - hashed storage;
  - a short expiry (state the value and why);
  - generation only by a server-side redirect handler, not by a client request, if `disableClientRequest` supports that shape.
- Add the redirect step. After the provider sign-in completes in the system browser, the server redirects to the app scheme callback with the token. The mobile card designs the shell half; this card only needs the server to emit the redirect for a registered app scheme.
- **Interception (human floor):** the plugin is not PKCE-bound to the attempt that started the sign-in. The PR must state how a callback intercepted by another app on the device is kept from being redeemed. One option is to bind the token to a verifier the shell generated, sent at the start and required at verify. The maintainer reviews and merges this PR.
- Declare the new public surface in `packages/spec`, as the contract-first rule requires. The spec lane owns that half.

## Who acts

The `domain:server` seat, with the spec half to the `domain:spec` seat. Triage first-touch decides the grade.

## Duplicate check (2026-11-03)

| Query | Hits |
| --- | --- |
| `is:issue oneTimeToken plugin` | 0 |
| `is:issue one-time-token` | 2121 tokenised hits, none on this plugin in the first page |
